title: add representative workload runners and reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We need a repeatable set of representative workload runners and a lightweight reporting pipeline to regularly surface regressions and unit economics delta across model/server/runtime permutations. This PR adds: (1) representative workload runners for TPU/GPU/CPU modes that mirror production traffic shapes, (2) a reporting pipeline that normalizes results across runs and pushes summaries to the benchmark-lab S3 bucket + a compact CSV for ingestion by the reporting dashboard, and (3) CI job integration to run a fast smoke of the representative runners on PRs that touch serving/runtime or benchmark code. Design notes: Runners are implemented as modular Python binaries under benchmark-lab/runners; each runner accepts a workload profile JSON and outputs a standardized result envelope (latency histogram, token throughput, error counts, and KV cache metrics). The reporting pipeline is a small Go binary and a YAML pipeline definition that aggregates run artifacts, computes baseline deltas, and emits both an artifacts.json and a summary CSV. The pipeline intentionally avoids heavy dependencies so it can run in our existing lightweight CI runners and on the perf lab. Backwards compatibility: Existing ad-hoc workload runners remain usable; this PR introduces a compatibility shim that translates legacy output into the new envelope. Rollout: Start with nightly runs in perf-canary, then enable PR smoke runs for redwood and benchmark-lab repos. Monitoring: Added alert thresholds to the reporting output to flag >5% median latency regressions or >10% throughput drop versus baseline. Testing: Unit tests for runner adapters and an integration test that runs the smallest representative profile in CI. Checklist: - [x] Add representative runners (gpu, cpu, tpu) - [x] Add reporting pipeline and YAML - [x] Add CI smoke job - [x] Add docs and README - [x] Add integration test - [x] Run perf-canary nightly for 3 days and validate outputs Changes are intentionally conservative in the runtime core: the runner uses the public serving API; no changes to the runtime kernel selection logic were required. Related: ENG-4871 (benchmarking roadmap), ENG-4920 (perf regression alerting).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice work. Can we make the default GPU profile use a slightly shorter context length for CI smoke runs? The current 2048 -> CI minutes are high.
Maya Chen (author): Agree, shortened the CI profile to 512 tokens for smoke runs. Kept 2048 as a perf-nightly default. Updated default_gpu_profile.json.
Lena Ortiz: The reporting pipeline looks good, but please add a TTL for artifacts in S3 (30 days) and redact any customer identifiers before upload.
Maya Chen (author): Added TTL and a simple redaction pass that strips request IDs and user metadata. The pipeline emits a redacted artifacts.json. Unit test added.
Samir Gupta: Minor: please split the large pipeline.go file into smaller packages; the monolith will be hard to maintain. Also add more comments on the baseline selection algorithm.
Maya Chen (author): Extracted baseline computation into reporting/baselines.go and added comments explaining the rolling-window baseline algorithm.
Tori Nakamura: Approved after requested changes. Integration test is passing locally and on CI after rerun (flaky seed fixed).
Arjun Patel: Approved. CI smoke job is lightweight and the nightly run produced expected CSVs in perf-canary bucket.

release_notes: Add representative workload runners and a lightweight reporting pipeline for benchmark-lab. Enables nightly aggregation of perf runs, PR smoke checks, and baseline delta alerts. No runtime-breaking changes.
notes: Nightly perf-canary runs started 2026-02-20; first 3-day run shows stable outputs. We will watch alerts for the next two weeks before enabling expanded profiles in release builds.
